analysis.investment_thesis: Unified Data fails nearly every quantitative filter I demand: P/E of 21.1 exceeds my 15 ceiling, ROE of 0.36% is effectively zero earning power, and the 6-digit BSE code suggests a recent listing with no multi-year earnings record. This is speculation on a small IT services story, not a value investment.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 60.39% signals committed ownership
Positive (if meager) earnings — not yet loss-making
Small-cap in an industry with structural tailwinds
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% — capital is earning nothing productive
P/E 21.1 prices in growth I cannot verify from history
Negligible institutional ownership (FII 0.57%, DII 5.89%) signals weak scrutiny
red_flags: Likely recent IPO — no multi-year earnings track record
ROE 0.36% suggests the 21x P/E is wildly disconnected from earning power
No disclosed book value, current ratio, debt, or dividend history — cannot compute Graham Number or margin of safety
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The central arithmetic is damning. A 21.1x P/E on a 0.36% ROE implies the market is capitalizing near-nonexistent earnings at a substantial premium — the opposite of the margin-of-safety equation I require. At ROE of 0.36%, earnings per rupee of equity are trivial; paying 21x for such earnings means the buyer is paying for a story, not for proven earning power. Without P/B, current ratio, debt-to-equity, or interest coverage disclosed, I cannot even construct a Graham Number — and the absence of those figures is itself a warning in Mr. Market's catalog.

The BSE 6-digit symbol and modest 619 Cr market cap are consistent with a recent SME-style listing, which by my doctrine is speculative by default: the seller knows more than the buyer. Combined with thin institutional ownership (under 6.5% FII+DII combined), no evidenced dividend history, and an ROE that cannot support reinvestment compounding, there is no foothold for the defensive investor. I would require several years of audited earnings above 10% ROE, a P/E below 15, P/B below 1.5, and current ratio above 2 before even opening the annual report again. Avoid.
